15%"). One POST to the v1beta generateContent endpoint of the Gemini API

runway never moves until a human clicks apply. A 3 second AbortSignal

clickable, and a rate limit never retries. The key comes from
`VITE_GEMINI_KEY` and travels only as the request header; it is never
printed or logged. The mode badge always shows whether the input came
from preset cards or a typed sentence.

**Why.** The twist card is spoken language, not sliders. Letting a judge
speak the shock removes UI friction in the 3 minute live twist, while the
engine's math never touches the model: the model only fills the same
typed twist struct the presets fill (`shockSpecToTwist` produces the same
`Twist` the preset cards produce), so every number still comes from the

36: ## Project Details
37: 
38: ##### Project Title:
39: Storm Fund: A resilience weather station for bank customers
40: 
41: ##### Elevator Pitch:
42: See your money move like weather. Storm Fund visualizes a bank account as a weather forecast. Anonymized bank data maps runway and buffer to a pixel sky. Inject a shock and watch the forecast change.
43: 
44: ## 4. About the project
45: 
46: Paste everything from "What inspired us" through the Links block into the
47: Devpost Description field. Devpost markdown supports headings, lists, bold,
48: links, and LaTeX math between dollar signs.
49: 
50: ### What inspired us
51: 
52: The Tangerine track, Resilience Rewired, asks for a financial resilience
53: engine for real bank customers: know the customer, take a shock, make a
54: plan, demonstrated live against real anonymized bank data. We read that as
55: building a weather forecasting system for personal finance. The judging
56: ritual set the design: a judge picks a random account id, reads a surprise
57: twist card you have never seen, and you answer live in about three
58: minutes. So the ask we designed around was plain: can a bank customer see
59: whether they survive a shock, and what saves them? Everyone knows what a
60: rainy day fund is; nobody has seen the rainy day coming. Bank numbers are
61: honest but unreadable, and a sky over the verdict band makes a shock
62: something you feel before it is something you calculate.
63: 
64: ### The question we asked
65: 
66: **The question.** How resilient are real account holders actually? We
67: asked a version a judge can check by hand: what share of accounts would
68: survive a month without income, and what does one surprise twist do to
69: that share?
70: 
71: **What we did.** We precomputed the judge's exact answer key metrics for
72: all 4,500 accounts (income, fixed costs, spending, buffer, household
73: bills, loan payment, plus gap and runway), built a live stress test
74: console with preset twist cards and custom shocks, and attached
75: prescriptive plans: an emergency fund goal plan and an ordered backup
76: lever ladder, every lever priced by re-running the same runway formula.
77: 
78: **What we found.** At baseline, 1 percent (60 of 4,500) of accounts sit
79: under 3 months of runway. Run the same 4,500 accounts through the laid
80: off twist (EI at 55 percent) and the count jumps to 10 percent (435 of
81: 4,500), so the storm zone share (critical plus storm warning, under 3
82: months) grows 10 times from one surprise card. The per account stories
83: keep the headline honest. Account 42988 already has a negative buffer and
84: a defaulted loan, so its baseline reads 0.0 months before any shock
85: lands. Account 98952 is a pensioner, so the layoff card is a stress test,
86: not a fact: there is no wage to lose. And 377 thin history accounts carry
87: medians that rest on fewer than 18 monthly rows, so the console says out
88: loud that the window is short.
89: 
90: ### What we learned
91: 
92: - **Judge parity is a design constraint, not an afterthought.** Our
93:   runway formula matches the answer key to the decimal, in integer cents,
94:   with the exact branch order (buffer left wins, then the no shortfall
95:   state, then the capped quotient). Every visual reads those numbers;
96:   none of them recompute them.
97: 
98:   $$\text{buffer}_{\text{left}} = B-C_{\text{one-off}}, \qquad
99:     \text{gap} = S'-I'$$
100: 
101:   $$\text{runway} =
102:     \begin{cases}
103:     0 & \text{if } \text{buffer}_{\text{left}} \le 0 \\
104:     \text{no shortfall (120+)} & \text{if } \text{gap} \le 0 \\
105:     \min\!\left(\frac{\text{buffer}_{\text{left}}}{\text{gap}},\ 120\right)
106:       & \text{otherwise, rounded to 1 decimal}
107:     \end{cases}$$
108: 
109: - **A weather skin stays honest only with a printed mapping legend.** Rain
110:   is income, evaporation is spending, water level is buffer. Say it on
111:   screen or the skin becomes decoration.
112: - **AI is a parser, not an oracle.** Gemini maps a typed shock sentence
113:   into the same typed fields the preset cards fill; a human confirms the
114:   chips before anything moves. The rules engine does the math. The model
115:   never touches the runway.
116: - **Accessibility and drama are the same problem.** Severity is carried by
117:   color and icon and text label, so the storm reads on a projector, on a
118:   laptop, and to a colorblind judge.
119: 
120: ### How we built it
121: 
122: - **Data:** the real anonymized bank dataset (4,500 accounts, 1.06M
123:   transactions, 185K monthly summaries, 682 loans), credited to the
124:   PKDD'99 Financial dataset via the CTU Prague Relational Dataset
125:   Repository.
126: - **Pipeline:** Python with pandas and numpy, fully vectorized (groupby,
127:   no per-account loops), integer cents throughout, `uv` for pinned
128:   dependencies. One pass produces `profiles.json` with the six judge
129:   metrics (I, F, S, B, H, P) plus a provenance check_sum for every
130:   number, and two consecutive builds are byte identical. An independent
131:   verifier recomputes all 4,500 accounts from the raw CSVs with the naive
132:   csv module (no pandas, no numpy) and diffs field by field, so drift
133:   fails the build, not the demo.
134: - **One formula, two languages, frozen fixtures:** the TypeScript twins of
135:   the Python formulas are pinned by shared golden fixtures asserted in
136:   both pytest and vitest, plus a cross check over all 4,500 profiles, so
137:   cross language drift becomes a failing test in either suite. Plans ride
138:   the same guard: `scripts/engine/golden_plans.json` is asserted from
139:   both sides.
140: - **Plans are re-runs, not new math:** each backup lever's "+N months"
141:   is a difference of two evaluations of the same runway function,
142:   $$\Delta m = m_{\text{runway}}(\text{after})\,-\,m_{\text{runway}}(\text{before})$$
143:   so every lever number is hand checkable against the printed formula.
144: - **Frontend:** React, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind. One derivation pass in
145:   the console view (inline money math in a component is a review
146:   failure), a pure `verdictBand` function maps runway to five verdict
147:   bands, and the forecast strip, bands, and EI cliff overlay are hand
148:   rolled SVG. All data bundled as JSON: zero runtime network calls, so
149:   the booth demo survives bad wifi.
150: - **Provenance and content rules:** every claim traces back through a
151:   check_sum over the account's own rows, and a dash scan keeps em dashes,
152:   en dashes, minus signs, double hyphens, and spaced hyphens out of the
153:   artifact and the site copy.
154: - **Entire:** a graph first workflow for concurrent multi agent
155:   development. Every session starts with `entire graph query`, commits
156:   carry an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, and `entire session tokens` keeps
157:   the cost visible.
158: - **Gemini (gated add-on):** a judge can type the shock in their own
159:   words ("EI covers half and the furnace dies"). One structured request

165: ### Challenges we faced
166: 
167: - **Answer key exactness.** Rounding rules a judge can hand check:
168:   medians over all rows (an even count averages the two middle cents half
169:   up), means and runway tenths with ties away from zero, and runway kept

171: - **Hostile random accounts.** A judge picks an id you have never seen
172:   and reads a twist card you cannot rehearse. Edge flags (thin history,
173:   negative buffer, zero income, defaulted loan, pension income, no loan,
174:   zero bills) inform the operator as chips and never gate an account: a

194: - **Honest deception discipline.** Provenance stamps say recorded, never
195:   verified, because the browser cannot recompute a check_sum without row

197:   ours. Solana receipts read bundled evidence only, with zero runtime
198:   RPC.
199: - **Scope under a 48 hour clock.** Weather particles are data driven or

205: Runway uses the answer key's definitions, including flat 55% EI (no weekly maximum, no taxes). 36: ## Project Details
37: 
38: ##### Project Title:
39: Storm Fund: A resilience weather station for bank customers
40: 
41: ##### Elevator Pitch:
42: See your money move like weather. Storm Fund visualizes a bank account as a weather forecast. Anonymized bank data maps runway and buffer to a pixel sky. Inject a shock and watch the forecast change.
43: 
44: ## 4. About the project
45: 
46: Paste everything from "What inspired us" through the Links block into the
47: Devpost Description field. Devpost markdown supports headings, lists, bold,
48: links, and LaTeX math between dollar signs.
49: 
50: ### What inspired us
51: 
52: The Tangerine track, Resilience Rewired, asks for a financial resilience
53: engine for real bank customers: know the customer, take a shock, make a
54: plan, demonstrated live against real anonymized bank data. We read that as
55: building a weather forecasting system for personal finance. The judging
56: ritual set the design: a judge picks a random account id, reads a surprise
57: twist card you have never seen, and you answer live in about three
58: minutes. So the ask we designed around was plain: can a bank customer see
59: whether they survive a shock, and what saves them? Everyone knows what a
60: rainy day fund is; nobody has seen the rainy day coming. Bank numbers are
61: honest but unreadable, and a sky over the verdict band makes a shock
62: something you feel before it is something you calculate.
63: 
64: ### The question we asked
65: 
66: **The question.** How resilient are real account holders actually? We
67: asked a version a judge can check by hand: what share of accounts would
68: survive a month without income, and what does one surprise twist do to
69: that share?
70: 
71: **What we did.** We precomputed the judge's exact answer key metrics for
72: all 4,500 accounts (income, fixed costs, spending, buffer, household
73: bills, loan payment, plus gap and runway), built a live stress test
74: console with preset twist cards and custom shocks, and attached
75: prescriptive plans: an emergency fund goal plan and an ordered backup
76: lever ladder, every lever priced by re-running the same runway formula.
77: 
78: **What we found.** At baseline, 1 percent (60 of 4,500) of accounts sit
79: under 3 months of runway. Run the same 4,500 accounts through the laid
80: off twist (EI at 55 percent) and the count jumps to 10 percent (435 of
81: 4,500), so the storm zone share (critical plus storm warning, under 3
82: months) grows 10 times from one surprise card. The per account stories
83: keep the headline honest. Account 42988 already has a negative buffer and
84: a defaulted loan, so its baseline reads 0.0 months before any shock
85: lands. Account 98952 is a pensioner, so the layoff card is a stress test,
86: not a fact: there is no wage to lose. And 377 thin history accounts carry
87: medians that rest on fewer than 18 monthly rows, so the console says out
88: loud that the window is short.
89: 
90: ### What we learned
91: 
92: - **Judge parity is a design constraint, not an afterthought.** Our
93:   runway formula matches the answer key to the decimal, in integer cents,
94:   with the exact branch order (buffer left wins, then the no shortfall
95:   state, then the capped quotient). Every visual reads those numbers;
96:   none of them recompute them.
97: 
98:   $$\text{buffer}_{\text{left}} = B-C_{\text{one-off}}, \qquad
99:     \text{gap} = S'-I'$$
100: 
101:   $$\text{runway} =
102:     \begin{cases}
103:     0 & \text{if } \text{buffer}_{\text{left}} \le 0 \\
104:     \text{no shortfall (120+)} & \text{if } \text{gap} \le 0 \\
105:     \min\!\left(\frac{\text{buffer}_{\text{left}}}{\text{gap}},\ 120\right)
106:       & \text{otherwise, rounded to 1 decimal}
107:     \end{cases}$$
108: 
109: - **A weather skin stays honest only with a printed mapping legend.** Rain
110:   is income, evaporation is spending, water level is buffer. Say it on
111:   screen or the skin becomes decoration.
112: - **AI is a parser, not an oracle.** Gemini maps a typed shock sentence
113:   into the same typed fields the preset cards fill; a human confirms the
114:   chips before anything moves. The rules engine does the math. The model
115:   never touches the runway.
116: - **Accessibility and drama are the same problem.** Severity is carried by
117:   color and icon and text label, so the storm reads on a projector, on a
118:   laptop, and to a colorblind judge.
119: 
120: ### How we built it
121: 
122: - **Data:** the real anonymized bank dataset (4,500 accounts, 1.06M
123:   transactions, 185K monthly summaries, 682 loans), credited to the
124:   PKDD'99 Financial dataset via the CTU Prague Relational Dataset
125:   Repository.
126: - **Pipeline:** Python with pandas and numpy, fully vectorized (groupby,
127:   no per-account loops), integer cents throughout, `uv` for pinned
128:   dependencies. One pass produces `profiles.json` with the six judge
129:   metrics (I, F, S, B, H, P) plus a provenance check_sum for every
130:   number, and two consecutive builds are byte identical. An independent
131:   verifier recomputes all 4,500 accounts from the raw CSVs with the naive
132:   csv module (no pandas, no numpy) and diffs field by field, so drift
133:   fails the build, not the demo.
134: - **One formula, two languages, frozen fixtures:** the TypeScript twins of
135:   the Python formulas are pinned by shared golden fixtures asserted in
136:   both pytest and vitest, plus a cross check over all 4,500 profiles, so
137:   cross language drift becomes a failing test in either suite. Plans ride
138:   the same guard: `scripts/engine/golden_plans.json` is asserted from
139:   both sides.
140: - **Plans are re-runs, not new math:** each backup lever's "+N months"
141:   is a difference of two evaluations of the same runway function,
142:   $$\Delta m = m_{\text{runway}}(\text{after})\,-\,m_{\text{runway}}(\text{before})$$
143:   so every lever number is hand checkable against the printed formula.
144: - **Frontend:** React, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind. One derivation pass in
145:   the console view (inline money math in a component is a review
146:   failure), a pure `verdictBand` function maps runway to five verdict
147:   bands, and the forecast strip, bands, and EI cliff overlay are hand
148:   rolled SVG. All data bundled as JSON: zero runtime network calls, so
149:   the booth demo survives bad wifi.
150: - **Provenance and content rules:** every claim traces back through a
151:   check_sum over the account's own rows, and a dash scan keeps em dashes,
152:   en dashes, minus signs, double hyphens, and spaced hyphens out of the
153:   artifact and the site copy.
154: - **Entire:** a graph first workflow for concurrent multi agent
155:   development. Every session starts with `entire graph query`, commits
156:   carry an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, and `entire session tokens` keeps
157:   the cost visible.
158: - **Gemini (gated add-on):** a judge can type the shock in their own
159:   words ("EI covers half and the furnace dies"). One structured request
160:   with a strict JSON schema returns typed fields, clamped and percent
161:   corrected in TypeScript, shown as confirmation chips with a formula
162:   strip. One click applies. A 3 second timeout falls back to preset
163:   cards, and the mode badge always shows where the input came from.
164: 
165: ### Challenges we faced
166: 
167: - **Answer key exactness.** Rounding rules a judge can hand check:
168:   medians over all rows (an even count averages the two middle cents half
169:   up), means and runway tenths with ties away from zero, and runway kept
170:   in integer tenths of a month. No float decides a branch.
171: - **Hostile random accounts.** A judge picks an id you have never seen
172:   and reads a twist card you cannot rehearse. Edge flags (thin history,
173:   negative buffer, zero income, defaulted loan, pension income, no loan,
174:   zero bills) inform the operator as chips and never gate an account: a
175:   property test walks every flagged id (over 500 of them) to prove
176:   selection still works.
177: - **The dataset was nine relational tables, not the single CSV the
178:   pipeline assumed.** We rebuilt the ingest around `monthly_summary.csv`
179:   (the judges' actual source) and kept `transactions.csv` (about 100 MB)
180:   out of the critical path.
181: - **Two vocabularies for one sky.** A parallel seven state ladder lived
182:   beside the five verdict bands. We resolved the conflict by deleting the
183:   ladder from code, artifacts, and docs so every surface speaks one
184:   vocabulary.
185: - **A stalled agent session.** An interrupted build session was cured
186:   with staged disk checkpoints: the work resumed from the modules already
187:   on disk, each checked against the checklist, which caught two rules
188:   that could never fire on real data (a thin history flag set below the
189:   shortest real history, and a fixture that cannot exist in this
190:   dataset).
191: - **Offline booth discipline.** Everything is bundled; the network is
192:   only a bonus. The Gemini path is the single exception and it aborts
193:   after 3 seconds into preset cards that stay clickable.
194: - **Honest deception discipline.** Provenance stamps say recorded, never
195:   verified, because the browser cannot recompute a check_sum without row
196:   data. Overlays beyond the answer key (the EI cliff) are labeled as
197:   ours. Solana receipts read bundled evidence only, with zero runtime
198:   RPC.
199: - **Scope under a 48 hour clock.** Weather particles are data driven or
200:   they do not ship. The cut order is written down, and the video and the
201:   write-up are never on it.
202: 
203: ### Limits we declare up front
204: 
205: Runway uses the answer key's definitions, including flat 55% EI (no weekly maximum, no taxes). Plans are our own declared formulas (goal = 3x spending), permitted by the brief and stated on screen. Correlation, not causation, everywhere. No customer rows leave the browser; the Gemini prompt carries a sentence and aggregate numbers only.
206: 
207: future work: a behavioral score attested on chain could gate a credit line or automate surplus sweeps; not implemented, and the underlying model (F3, AUC 0.590) is not strong enough to gate credit
208:

214: - Reproduce: `uv sync`, then `uv run python -m scripts.engine.build`,

217: ## 4b. Generative AI question
218: 
219: Question on the form: Did you implement a generative AI model or API in
220: your hack this weekend? If so, how and why did you use it? If not, mark
221: your response as N/A.
222: 
223: **Answer: yes. One generative AI integration, the Gemini API for typed
224: shock input.**
225: 
226: **How.** A judge types the shock as a sentence ("laid off and rent up
227: 15%"). One POST to the v1beta generateContent endpoint of the Gemini API
228: (`generativelanguage.googleapis.com`, pinned model
229: `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`) sends the sentence plus the account id and the
230: six baseline metrics as integer cents, at temperature 0, with a strict
231: JSON responseSchema (`additionalProperties: false`, seven required keys:
232: intent, confidence, incomeFactor, billsPct, oneOffMonths, durationMonths,
233: summary), so the typed twist struct the app expects is the guaranteed
234: output shape. TypeScript then shape checks, percent corrects, clamps, and
235: rounds every field, shows the result as confirmation chips with a formula
236: strip of the dollar arithmetic, and a mandatory confirm gate
237: (`confirmTypedShock`, the only path into twist state) applies it. The
238: runway never moves until a human clicks apply. A 3 second AbortSignal
239: timeout falls back to the preset twist cards, which stay rendered and
240: clickable, and a rate limit never retries. The key comes from
241: `VITE_GEMINI_KEY` and travels only as the request header; it is never
242: printed or logged. The mode badge always shows whether the input came
243: from preset cards or a typed sentence.
244: 
245: **Why.** The twist card is spoken language, not sliders. Letting a judge
246: speak the shock removes UI friction in the 3 minute live twist, while the
247: engine's math never touches the model: the model only fills the same
248: typed twist struct the presets fill (`shockSpecToTwist` produces the same
249: `Twist` the preset cards produce), so every number still comes from the
250: deterministic integer cents engine. Privacy boundary: the prompt carries
251: the sentence, the account id, and six aggregate baseline figures as plain
252: numbers; no raw rows or transaction history leave the browser.

The file looks good. A few refinements to consider:

1. Line 205 (Limits) and line 207 (E7 sentence): preserved byte identical? Line 207 matches original line 104 exactly (verify by comparing: original: "future work: a behavioral score attested on chain could gate a credit line or automate surplus sweeps; not implemented, and the underlying model (F3, AUC 0.590) is not strong enough to gate credit"). Yes matches.

2. Check "no em dashes" etc: grep showed only table separators. Also non-ASCII grep: no matches. Good.

3. Potential issue: line 140-143, the display math inside a bullet immediately after a comma, followed by a continuation line "so every lever number..." - the math block is inline within a paragraph of a list item. In markdown, "$$...$$" on its own line inside a paragraph... CommonMark will treat lines as one paragraph (lazy continuation) since no blank lines. MathJax processes $$...$$ across lines within paragraphs. Should render. But there's a subtlety: the line after the closing $$ is a continuation of the same paragraph - fine.

Actually wait, one risk: line 142 starts with two spaces "  $$\Delta..." - it's a continuation line of the bullet paragraph (bullet content indent = 2). Good.

4. "the count jumps to 10 percent (435 of 4,500)" - saying "count jumps to 10 percent" is slightly off (count jumps to 435, share to 10 percent). Let me fix wording: "the share jumps to 10 percent (435 of 4,500)". Edit line 80: "off twist (EI at 55 percent) and the count jumps to 10 percent (435 of" → "off twist (EI at 55 percent) and the share jumps to 10 percent (435 of".Better: "and the count jumps to 435 of 4,500, which is 10 percent". Simpler edit: change "the count jumps to 10 percent" to "the share jumps to 10 percent".

5. Check the elevator pitch says "168 of 200 characters" - unrelated.

6. Section 4b heading "## 4b." consistent with paste map. Good.

7. One more accuracy check: "185K monthly summaries" - profiles meta rows 185326. OK.

8. "a property test walks every flagged id (over 500 of them)" - reviews says over 500. Good.

9. "EI cliff overlay" - architecture says "EI-cliff overlay labeled beyond the answer key" (with hyphen EI-cliff). I wrote "EI cliff overlay" and "(the EI cliff)". Fine.

10. "hand rolled SVG" - fine.

11. "Both pytest and vitest" for golden fixtures: verify claim "shared golden fixtures asserted in both pytest and vitest" - decisions E1/E4: golden fixtures asserted by tests in both; golden_plans.json asserted by both vitest and pytest (architecture E4: "goldens in scripts/engine/golden_plans.json asserted by both vitest and pytest"). And shocks goldens: architecture verification says "uv run pytest -q: golden fixtures..." and "npx vitest run: ... shock/plan/forecast twins over shared goldens, 4500 profile cross checks". Good.

12. "plus a cross check over all 4,500 profiles" - vitest "4500 profile cross checks". Good.

13. "two consecutive builds are byte identical" - decisions E1. Good.

14. "naive csv module (no pandas, no numpy)" - decisions E1: "recomputes all 4500 accounts with the naive csv module (no pandas, no numpy, no import of metrics)". Good. Also I said verifier "diffs field by field" - decisions: "diffs field by field". Good.

"rate limit never retries" verified (429 returns rejected, comment "exactly one fetch is ever attempted (429 never retries)"). "key ... never printed or logged" - logResponse logs hash/latency/raw/validated/cached; key used only in header. Defensible. "the only path into twist state" for confirmTypedShock - decisions: "pendingShock is the only state the typed path writes: confirmTypedShock is the single gate into twist." ## Documentation: Devpost submission doc (docs/devpost.md)

### Files Modified
| File | Action | Purpose |
|------|--------|---------|
| `docs/devpost.md` | updated | Rewrote section 4 as the actual submission story; added section 4b with the generative AI answer; added paste-map row and draft-checklist item for 4b |

### Content Summary

**Section 4 "About the project" (before → after)**

- **What inspired us** (before: reservoir/rain metaphor plus Terraria pixel art lore) → (after: the Resilience Rewired challenge framing, our reading of it as a weather forecasting system for personal finance, the judging ritual of a random account id plus an unread twist card answered live, and the ask: can a bank customer see whether they survive a shock and what saves them; keeps the rainy day idiom and "bank numbers are honest but unreadable").
- **New subsection "The question we asked"** (Discovery narrative): **The question** (how resilient are real account holders, what share would survive a month without income, what does one twist do), **What we did** (answer-key metrics precomputed for all 4,500 accounts, live stress-test console with preset and custom shocks, prescriptive plans: goal plan plus ordered backup lever ladder), **What we found** (1 percent, 60 of 4,500 under 3 months at baseline; 10 percent, 435 of 4,500 under the laid off twist, EI at 55 percent; storm zone share grows 10 times; per account stories: 42988 negative buffer plus defaulted loan reading 0.0 months at baseline, 98952 pensioner where the layoff card is a stress test not a fact, 377 thin history accounts with medians on fewer than 18 rows).
- **What we learned** (before: 4 bullets, one non-branching LaTeX formula, "no-shortfall" hyphenated, Gemini "three numbers") → (after: same 4 bullets refreshed; branch-accurate LaTeX: `buffer_left = B-C_one-off`, `gap = S'-I'`, and a `\begin{cases}` block for runway with the three branch rules; Gemini bullet now says "the same typed fields the preset cards fill").
- **How we built it** (before: 4 bullets; verifier claimed "a seeded sample", "chunked reads", `React,Vite`) → (after: 7 bullets: data credit; pipeline with byte-identical rebuilds and an independent naive csv verifier over all 4,500 accounts; one formula in two languages pinned by shared goldens asserted in both pytest and vitest; lever math as LaTeX difference of two runway evaluations `$\Delta m = m_{runway}(after)\,-\,m_{runway}(before)$`; frontend with one derivation pass; provenance check_sums plus the dash-scan content rule; Entire graph-first workflow; gated Gemini add-on).
- **Challenges we faced** (before: 4 bullets including the now false "chunked reads" claim) → (after: 8 bullets: answer-key exactness with the rounding rules, hostile random accounts with guards that inform and never gate plus the property test over flagged ids, nine relational tables, the seven state ladder deleted for one vocabulary, the stalled agent session cured with staged disk checkpoints, offline booth discipline with the 3 second Gemini abort, honest-deception discipline (recorded vs verified provenance, beyond-the-answer-key labels, zero runtime RPC receipts), scope under a 48 hour clock).
- **Limits we declare up front**: paragraph kept byte identical (all four limits still true); the E7 future-work sentence kept byte exact at line 207; **Links** unchanged.

**Section 4b "Generative AI question" (new; no answer slot existed)**: placed after section 4, before section 5, in the form-answer region; added paste-map row `| 4b. Generative AI question | ... |` and a draft checklist item `[ ] Generative AI answer pasted (section 4b)`.

**Exact AI answer text** (paste this into the form):

> **Answer: yes. One generative AI integration, the Gemini API for typed shock input.**
>
> **How.** A judge types the shock as a sentence ("laid off and rent up 15%"). One POST to the v1beta generateContent endpoint of the Gemini API (`generativelanguage.googleapis.com`, pinned model `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`) sends the sentence plus the account id and the six baseline metrics as integer cents, at temperature 0, with a strict JSON responseSchema (`additionalProperties: false`, seven required keys: intent, confidence, incomeFactor, billsPct, oneOffMonths, durationMonths, summary), so the typed twist struct the app expects is the guaranteed output shape. TypeScript then shape checks, percent corrects, clamps, and rounds every field, shows the result as confirmation chips with a formula strip of the dollar arithmetic, and a mandatory confirm gate (`confirmTypedShock`, the single gate into twist state) applies it. The runway never moves until a human clicks apply. A 3 second AbortSignal timeout falls back to the preset twist cards, which stay rendered and clickable, and a rate limit never retries. The key comes from `VITE_GEMINI_KEY` and travels only as the request header; it is never printed or logged. The mode badge always shows whether the input came from preset cards or a typed sentence.
>
> **Why.** The twist card is spoken language, not sliders. Letting a judge speak the shock removes UI friction in the 3 minute live twist, while the engine's math never touches the model: the model only fills the same typed twist struct the presets fill (`shockSpecToTwist` produces the same `Twist` the preset cards produce), so every number still comes from the deterministic integer cents engine. Privacy boundary: the prompt carries the sentence, the account id, and six aggregate baseline figures as plain numbers; no raw rows or transaction history leave the browser.

- **42988 defaulted loan plus negative buffer, baseline 0.0 months**: `docs/reviews.md:231` (fixture 42988), guard copy `src/lib/judgeMode.ts:280`.
- **98952 pensioner stress test wording**: `src/lib/judgeMode.ts:288-289`, fixture list `docs/reviews.md:231`, `docs/decisions.md:230`.
- **377 thin history accounts, fewer than 18 monthly rows**: `docs/decisions.md:222-223`, `docs/profiles-schema.md:38`, guard copy `src/lib/judgeMode.ts:278-279`.
- **Edge flags inform, never gate; over 500 flagged ids walked**: `docs/architecture.md:83`, `docs/reviews.md:230`.
- **Rounding rules (half up medians, ties away from zero, integer tenths)**: `public/data/engine/profiles.json` meta `rounding` string, `docs/profiles-schema.md:34-36`.
- **Naive csv verifier over all 4,500, byte identical builds, fixture coverage**: `docs/decisions.md:225-237`; verifier module `scripts/engine/verify.py`.
- **Goldens asserted in both pytest and vitest, 4,500 profile cross check**: `docs/architecture.md:168-177`, `docs/decisions.md:330-333`.
- **Seven state ladder deleted, one five band vocabulary**: `docs/architecture.md:32-36`, `docs/reviews.md:214`, AGENTS.md coordination note.
- **Recorded vs verified provenance, beyond-the-answer-key labels, zero runtime RPC receipts**: `docs/architecture.md:67, 110-111, 119-121`, `docs/decisions.md:284-285`.
- **Gemini facts (model, endpoint, schema, temperature 0, 3 s abort, VITE_GEMINI_KEY, confirm gate)**: `src/lib/shockParse.ts:23-26, 137-138, 197-219, 302-322, 654`, `src/components/console/TypedShock.tsx`, `docs/decisions.md:287-310`.
- **Dataset sizes (4,500 / 1.06M / 185K / 682 loans), nine tables, 100 MB transactions**: `docs/tangerine-challenge.md:13, 105-150`, `docs/profiles-schema.md:32-39`.
- **E7 sentence**: verified byte exact at `docs/devpost.md:207`.
